bounded_statement: For this submission only: the selected result (exact two-sided binomial test, 15 warm choices in 20 releases, p = 0.0414, reported as evidence of a warm-arm preference) treats all 20 CSV rows as independent Bernoulli trials, but the declared independent unit is salamander_id and only 5 animals exist, each contributing 4 repeated releases. The observed data show strong within-animal clustering (three animals chose warm 4/4, one chose cool 3/4), and any animal-level summary (3 warm-preferring vs 1 cool-preferring animals, 1 tied) is nowhere near significance at the 5% level. The stated statistical conclusion is therefore not supported by an analysis that respects the declared independent unit.

counterevidence_considered.description: The data description itself says 'One trial is: one row', which could be read as authorizing row-level trials; however, this defines the row semantics, not statistical independence, and the same description names salamander_id as the independent-unit column.

The design swapped warm and cool arms between days, which rules out a fixed side preference as the driver of the pattern; this mitigates side-bias confounding but does nothing to remove the dependence among the four releases of the same animal.

evidence.description: The raw data show strong within-animal clustering: SAL-01, SAL-02, and SAL-03 chose warm on all four releases, while SAL-04 chose cool on three of four; rows from the same animal are visibly not independent.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defend the pooled analysis two ways. (1) If within-animal releases were effectively independent, per-animal choice sequences should look like independent coin flips of a shared warm probability; instead three of five animals are 4/4 warm and one is 3/4 cool, extreme clustering by salamander_id that contradicts the row-independence assumption on the observed data themselves. (2) I re-ran the inference at the declared independent unit: classifying each animal by majority choice gives 3 warm-preferring, 1 cool-preferring, 1 tied (SAL-05 at 2/2); an exact two-sided binomial/sign test on the 4 non-tied animals gives p = 0.625, and even the most favorable animal-level reading (4 of 5 animals warm-leaning) gives p = 0.375. I also verified the reported pooled value, binomtest(15, 20, 0.5) two-sided p ≈ 0.0414, so the report's numbers are internally correct but the significance claim vanishes under any unit-respecting analysis. Both defenses fail, so the issue stands.

root_cause: The workflow tallies warm choices across every row of data/input.csv and submits the pooled count directly to scipy.stats.binomtest(n_warm, n_total, 0.5), a procedure whose null distribution assumes each of the 20 rows is an independent trial. Because each of the 5 salamanders (the declared independent unit, salamander_id) is entered 4 times, within-animal correlation in arm choice inflates the effective sample size from 5 to 20 and shrinks the p-value; the code never groups by salamander_id or otherwise models the repeated entries.
